title: A 26-Year-Old YouTuber Made a $750K Horror Film. It Just Crossed $371 Million.
excerpt: Curry Barker's Obsession dethroned Sinners to become the highest-grossing live-action original of the 2020s — and it streams on Prime Video and Apple TV starting today
body:
There is no universe in which this story should have happened.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=gMC8kkwbIQQ</youtube>

A horror movie made for less than the price of a decent flat in Bandra. Directed by a 26-year-old who was posting sketch comedy on YouTube when most filmmakers his age are still begging for meetings. A cast of unknowns. No franchise. No IP. No safety net.

And yet **Obsession**, Curry Barker's supernatural love story-slash-nightmare, just closed its seventh weekend in theatres with a cumulative global haul of **$371.2 million** — officially overtaking Ryan Coogler's **Sinners** ($370.3 million) to become the **highest-grossing live-action English-language original movie of the 2020s**.

Read that number again. $371 million. On a budget that reportedly came in under **$750,000**.

> "The wish is simple. The cost isn't."

The film follows **Bear** (**Michael Johnston**), a lovesick teenager who breaks a branch from a mysterious "One Wish Willow" to make the girl he is obsessed with, **Nikki** (**Inde Navarrette**), fall for him. She does. Completely. Suffocatingly. The wish works — and then it keeps working, mutating desire into possession, love into something with teeth. What starts as a teen romance curdles into body horror with a precision that would make Ari Aster sweat.

## The Numbers That Don't Make Sense



> **""I'm not saying it has to be five, six years from now," he said."**


**Obsession** opened to a modest $17.2 million domestically — a fine start, not a firework. Then something happened that hasn't occurred in American cinema since **1982**: each of the film's first three weekends earned *more* than the one before it. Word of mouth didn't just build — it compounded. Since then, the film has never dropped more than 30% week-over-week, a retention rate that theatrical distributors describe in reverent whispers.

The critical response has matched the commercial performance. A **96% on Rotten Tomatoes** from critics. **94% from audiences**. An **A- CinemaScore** — extraordinary for horror, a genre that typically lives in the B range. Blumhouse, the production house behind *Get Out* and *The Purge*, produced it through Focus Features, and even they seem mildly stunned by the outcome.

In India, **Obsession** has grossed approximately **₹97.5 crore** and is days away from crossing the **₹100 crore** mark — which would make it the **highest-grossing Hollywood horror film in Indian theatrical history**, surpassing *The Conjuring: Last Rites* (₹101.65 crore). For a film with no Indian stars, no Hindi dub, and no festival-circuit buildup, that number is astonishing.


![Ryan Coogler — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/99/Ryan_Coogler_-_Sinners_2025_%28cropped%29.jpg)


## The Man Behind It

The most outrageous part of this story might be its director. **Curry Barker** is 26 years old. He built his following on YouTube, posting short-form comedy sketches that leaned into absurdist horror before horror was cool on the internet. *Obsession* is his feature debut. He had no agents pushing him into rooms, no generational wealth funding the production, no studio development deal. He made a movie, and 371 million dollars later, he is the most bankable director in Hollywood by any return-on-investment metric that matters.

At a roughly **49,000% return on investment**, *Obsession* sits alongside *Paranormal Activity* and *The Blair Witch Project* in the pantheon of micro-budget horror miracles — except it has already outgrossed both of them.

And he is not done. In a recent interview with *The Hollywood Reporter*, Barker confirmed he will direct an **Obsession sequel** — though not immediately. "I'm not saying it has to be five, six years from now," he said. "But I think people would be just as excited for it if it came a little down the road." Before that, he has two other projects lined up: *Anything But Ghosts* and A24's *Texas Chainsaw Massacre*.

## Where to Watch — Starting Today

For diaspora audiences who missed *Obsession* in theatres — or who want to experience the uncut version from the couch — the wait is finally over. **Focus Features has confirmed that the film arrives on VOD platforms, including Apple TV and Prime Video, on June 30.** That is today.

The VOD release is expected to be available in the US, UK, and Canada. An official Indian streaming date has not been confirmed yet, though the theatrical cut continues to play in cinemas across the country. Indian viewers may need to wait for a separate announcement, but the global VOD drop means diaspora audiences can watch it tonight.

If you haven't seen it yet: clear the evening. Dim the lights. And maybe watch with someone — you will want a hand to hold.

## Why This Matters

*Obsession* is not just a box office story. It is a referendum on what audiences actually want — and what studios have been getting wrong for years. No CGI spectacle. No shared universe. No legacy IP. Just a tightly wound, emotionally devastating horror film made by someone who understood that the scariest thing in the world is wanting someone too much.

In a summer dominated by franchise sequels and ₹300-crore star vehicles, a $750K movie made by a YouTube comedian just ate all of them alive. Bollywood, Hollywood, and everyone else making movies should be taking notes.

*Obsession is now streaming on Apple TV and Prime Video.*
